worldcombat.skill.skydrop.summary: Grab an adjacent foe, haul it into the sky for a while (it cannot act up there), then slam it into the ground; the higher you carry it and the heavier it is, the harder it lands. A foe too heavy to lift leaves the move unlaunched.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.use.0: Take a key target out of the fight for a moment
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.use.1: Grab an adjacent foe and slam it back down
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.use.2: Trade a heavy slam for time exposed in the air
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.description.0: The slam deals about %1$s damage; the actual lift height multiplies it, and the target's defence, type matchup and criticals settle at impact.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.description.1: Only a target weighing up to %1$s kg can be lifted; a heavier one is refused before commit and spends no PP.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.description.2: The target is lifted to %1$s and held for %2$s; while held it cannot act.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.description.3: You must close to %1$s blocks to grab; rise at %2$s blocks per tick and drop at %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.high.on: Carry high on: lifted higher and held longer, slam about x1.15, but slower to start and longer cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.high.off: Carry high off (quick low toss): lifted lower and slam about x0.85, but faster to recover and shorter cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.timing: Castable on a target within %1$s blocks; after a %2$s s prepare it spends %4$s PP; it recovers for %3$s s and its cooldown starts on commit for %5$s s.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.growth.0: At level %1$s the slam's power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.growth.1: At level %1$s the slam's power rises to %2$s and the lift height to %3$s.
worldcombat.skill.skydrop.preference.car: On: lifted higher and held longer, slam about x1.15, but +3 ticks to start and +10 ticks cooldown. Off (quick low toss): lifted lower and slam about x0.85, but faster to recover and shorter cooldown.
The companion considers Sky Drop only when a threat is this close; lower grabs only adjacent foes, higher chases further first.
Only targets up to this weight (kg) are attempted; lower grabs only light foes, higher risks a failed lift on a heavy one.
On: a target with no other foe within 4 blocks is strongly preferred, taking it out of the fight; off: ordinary attack ordering.
